title: Delete user
text: As an admin, I can delete a user account via DELETE /users/{id}.

acs.AC1: An admin calling DELETE /users/{id} with a valid id receives 204 and the user is no longer retrievable.
acs.AC2: Calling with a non-existent id returns 404.
acs.AC3: The user's owned projects are reassigned to the workspace owner, not deleted.
acs.AC4: Deletion is recorded in the audit log with the acting admin's id.

title: Create project
text: As a workspace member, I can create a project via POST /projects.

acs.AC1: A request with a valid name and workspace_id returns 201 with the created project.
acs.AC2: Project names must be 1-80 characters; violations return 422.
acs.AC3: Duplicate project name within the same workspace returns 409.
acs.AC4: The creator is automatically assigned the project owner role.

title: Retrieve order
text: As a customer, I can retrieve one of my orders via GET /orders/{id}.

acs.AC1: A customer retrieving their own order receives 200 with full order detail.
acs.AC2: A customer retrieving another customer's order receives 404, not 403, to avoid leaking existence.
acs.AC3: Cancelled orders are still retrievable and show status cancelled.
acs.AC4: The response includes line items ordered by their original sequence.

title: Update invoice status
text: As a finance user, I can update an invoice status via PATCH /invoices/{id}.

acs.AC1: Allowed transitions are draft to sent, sent to paid, and sent to void.
acs.AC2: Any other transition returns 409 with the current and attempted status.
acs.AC3: Transitioning to paid records the payment timestamp.
acs.AC4: A paid invoice is immutable; further PATCH returns 409.

title: Share document
text: As a document owner, I can share a document via POST /documents/{id}/share.

acs.AC1: Sharing with a valid user email and permission level returns 201.
acs.AC2: Permission level must be one of viewer, commenter, editor; others return 422.
acs.AC3: Sharing a document you do not own returns 403.
acs.AC4: Re-sharing with an existing recipient updates their permission rather than creating a duplicate.

title: Password reset
text: As a user who forgot my password, I can reset it using an emailed token.

acs.AC1: Requesting a reset for a registered email sends a single-use token valid for 30 minutes.
acs.AC2: Requesting a reset for an unregistered email returns the same success response, to avoid account enumeration.
acs.AC3: Using a token more than once returns an error and does not change the password.
acs.AC4: A successful reset invalidates all existing sessions for that user.

title: Role change propagation
text: As a workspace admin, I can change a member's role and have it take effect immediately.

acs.AC1: Demoting an editor to viewer immediately blocks their write endpoints.
acs.AC2: An admin cannot demote themselves if they are the last remaining admin.
acs.AC3: Role changes are written to the audit log with before and after values.
acs.AC4: In-flight requests authorized under the old role are not retroactively failed.

title: Session expiry and refresh
text: As a signed-in user, my session refreshes silently until the absolute expiry is reached.

acs.AC1: An access token expiring within 60 seconds is refreshed transparently using a valid refresh token.
acs.AC2: A refresh token reused after rotation invalidates the whole token family.
acs.AC3: After the 30-day absolute expiry, refresh fails and the user must sign in again.
acs.AC4: Signing out revokes both the access and refresh tokens.

title: MFA enrollment
text: As a user, I can enrol in TOTP-based multi-factor authentication.

acs.AC1: Enrolment shows a QR code and requires one correct code before MFA is activated.
acs.AC2: Ten single-use recovery codes are issued at activation and shown exactly once.
acs.AC3: Codes from the adjacent 30-second window are accepted to allow for clock drift.
acs.AC4: Disabling MFA requires re-entering the account password.

title: API key revocation
text: As an account owner, I can revoke an API key and stop its access immediately.

acs.AC1: A revoked key returns 401 on the next request, with no caching grace period.
acs.AC2: Revocation is irreversible; the key cannot be reactivated.
acs.AC3: The key's last-used timestamp and request count remain visible after revocation.
acs.AC4: Only the account owner or the key's creator can revoke it.

title: Signup form
text: As a visitor, I can create an account using the signup form.

acs.AC1: Email, password, and accepted-terms checkbox are required before submit is enabled.
acs.AC2: Password strength is shown live and must reach at least the medium threshold.
acs.AC3: An already-registered email shows an inline error without clearing the form.
acs.AC4: Validation errors are announced to screen readers and associated with their field.

title: Checkout address form
text: As a shopper, I can enter a shipping address during checkout.

acs.AC1: Required fields are line 1, city, postal code, and country.
acs.AC2: Postal code format validation changes with the selected country.
acs.AC3: Selecting a saved address autofills all fields and keeps them editable.
acs.AC4: Navigating back from the payment step preserves entered values.

title: Bulk CSV upload
text: As an operations user, I can bulk-import contacts by uploading a CSV file.

acs.AC1: Only .csv files up to 10 MB are accepted; others are rejected before upload starts.
acs.AC2: A preview of the first 5 rows with detected column mapping is shown before import.
acs.AC3: Rows that fail validation are reported with row numbers and the valid rows still import.
acs.AC4: Upload progress is shown and the import can be cancelled mid-flight.

title: Profile settings
text: As a user, I can update my profile details and avatar.

acs.AC1: Display name is required and limited to 50 characters.
acs.AC2: Avatar accepts PNG or JPEG up to 2 MB and is cropped to a square before upload.
acs.AC3: Leaving the page with unsaved changes prompts for confirmation.
acs.AC4: Changing the email address requires confirming via a link sent to the new address.

title: Support ticket form
text: As a customer, I can submit a support ticket with attachments.

acs.AC1: Subject and description are required; category defaults to General.
acs.AC2: Up to 3 attachments of 5 MB each are allowed.
acs.AC3: Submitting twice by double-clicking creates only one ticket.
acs.AC4: On success the user sees the ticket reference number.

title: Split full_name
text: Migrate the users table by splitting full_name into first_name and last_name.

acs.AC1: Existing full_name values are split on the last space into first_name and last_name.
acs.AC2: Single-token names populate first_name and leave last_name empty rather than failing.
acs.AC3: The migration is idempotent and safe to re-run.
acs.AC4: full_name is retained until a follow-up release, and both are kept in sync during the transition.

title: Backfill tenant_id
text: Backfill tenant_id on legacy rows in the documents table and make the column non-nullable.

acs.AC1: Every existing document is assigned the tenant_id of its owning user.
acs.AC2: Documents with no resolvable owner are moved to a quarantine table rather than assigned a default tenant.
acs.AC3: The non-null constraint is added only after the backfill verifies zero remaining nulls.
acs.AC4: The migration runs in batches and does not hold a long table lock.

title: Currency to minor units
text: Convert the amount column on payments from float dollars to integer minor units.

acs.AC1: Each float amount is converted to integer cents using half-up rounding.
acs.AC2: The sum of converted amounts is reconciled against the original sum and the migration aborts on mismatch beyond one cent per row.
acs.AC3: Currencies with zero minor units, such as JPY, are handled without multiplying by 100.
acs.AC4: A rollback path restores the original float column from a retained copy.

title: Merge duplicate customers
text: Merge duplicate customer records identified by matching normalized email.

acs.AC1: The oldest record is kept as the survivor and other records' orders are reparented to it.
acs.AC2: Conflicting non-empty field values are resolved by most-recently-updated wins.
acs.AC3: A merge audit row records every source id folded into the survivor.
acs.AC4: Merges are performed in a transaction per duplicate group so a failure affects only that group.

title: Timestamps to UTC
text: Convert timezone-naive timestamps in the events table to timezone-aware UTC.

acs.AC1: Existing naive values are interpreted as the recorded server timezone and converted to UTC.
acs.AC2: Rows spanning a daylight-saving transition are converted using the correct offset for their date.
acs.AC3: The migration records the source timezone assumption in a schema comment.
acs.AC4: Application reads during the migration return correct values for both converted and unconverted rows.
